newsitem.title: USA: Miami still lacks creditworthiness - bond official.
newsitem.headline: Miami still lacks creditworthiness - bond official.

text.p: Miami, Fla., lacks the creditworthiness to enter the public debt market and probably could not obtain favorable rates on the private market, Florida bond chief Ben Watkins said Monday.
The state oversight board guiding Miami's fiscal recovery asked Watkins to review the city's budget plan and comment on its prospects for restoring credit market access.
"The city of Miami could not go out and borrow on a long-term basis now" and "probably does not have short-term access" in the public market, Watkins said.
While the city could issue short-term notes via a private offering to local banks "They've still got a long way to go in terms of rates that would be acceptable," Watkins told the board.

The comments by Watkins, director of the Florida Division of Bond Finance, cast doubts on the city's tentative plan to issue about $20 million of tax anticipation notes in October via a private placement with local banks.
Fortunately, Watkins told Reuters after the oversight board meeting, the city's latest cash flow projections indicate the sale would be unnecessary.
"They don't need to do any short-term borrowing," he said.

Moody's Investors Service and Standard & Poors Corp have cut Miami's general obligation bond ratings to non-investment grade because of its recurring deficits. A plan submitted to the oversight board eliminates the deficits.
But Watson said the city would have to set budget benchmarks and then show that it could meet them before the municipal market regains confidence in Miami.

City Manager Ed Marquez disagreed with Watkins' assertion that private borrowing rates would be prohibitive, but acknowledged the public market was out of reach at least until after a September referendum on whether to dissolve the city.
"We wholeheartedly agree with him that the proof is in the pudding. We have to show some progress," Marquez said. "It's going to take a lot of work."
